newsitem.title: USA: Equitable of Iowa settles suit, sees charge.
newsitem.headline: Equitable of Iowa settles suit, sees charge.

text.p: Equitable of Iowa Cos said Friday it agreed to settle a class-action lawsuit regarding the sale and performance of certain life insurance policies issued by the company between 1984 and 1996.

Equitable expects to accrue an expense of about $20 million, or about $13 million on an after-tax basis for policy liabilities and administrative and other costs expected with the proposed settlement. The accrual will reduce net income per share after tax by about $0.40 for its second quarter ended June 30, 1997.
Subject to court approval, a hearing regarding final approval of the settlement is expected to be scheduled for near the end of this year, Equitable said.
According to Equitable of Iowa Chairman and President Fred Hubbell, the company denies the allegations in the lawsuit, which has been pending in some form since mid-1995.

"Further defense against the lawsuit would likely continue to be costly and disruptive to the management and operation of our businesses," said Hubbell. "We are agreeing to this settlement to limit further expense and burden on our operations. We admit to no wrongdoing, but we plan to act in the best interests of all our customers."

The lawsuit's primary allegations cover the use of policy values to pay annual premiums; monthly deductions charged against policies; and marketing practices, such as the replacement of policies and the sales of insurance as a retirement vehicle.

The company expects the $20 million to cover anticipated expenses from the settlement. Future expenses, if any, are not expected to impact the company's profitability going forward and ongoing operations will not be affected by this charge, the company said.

According to the proposed settlement, owners of about 130,000 life insurance policies issued by the company from 1984 through 1996 may be eligible to receive certain benefits. They include a one-time enhancement to the interest component of the policy, a one-time enhancement to the dividend component of the policy and optional premium loans that would allow policyholders to borrow at reduced rates.
The company will notify all affected policyholders through notices mailed by September 30.
